newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Saudi Aramco loses Japan Super Light lifters - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco loses Japan Super Light lifters - MEES.

text.p: State-owned Saudi Aramco now has only one Japanese term customer for its Arab Super Light (ASL) crude after a number of lifters declined to renew contract volumes for the high quality oil, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
"MEES understands that a number of Japanese customers elected not to renew their ASL commitments when contract terms came up for review at the end of last year," the newsletter said.

"The exodus leaves Taiyo Oil the only remaining ASL contract customer in Japan...(Taiyo) has lifted 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) of ASL since the crude was first introduced in November 1994," the Cyprus-based MEES said.
The loss of Japanese contract lifters has prompted Aramco to supply more than half of the 200,000 bpd ASL to its joint venture refinery in South Korea.
Aramco's other term ASL contracts are limited to individual contracts in South Korea which are below 10,000 bpd.
Plans to increase production capacity at ASL fields in central Saudi Arabia were shelved late last year.

ASL was promoted by Aramco as a way of increasing the country's oil revenue since the company could seek higher prices in the market because of the potentially high yields and low sulphur quantity of ASL.
ASL exports to the Far East for October lifting are priced at a $2.40 a barrel premium to the regional price markers of Oman and Dubai crude.
